- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) and forecast shows a sharp downward spike, reduce the magnitude of the drop to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.23) and forecast rises sharply, cap the upward momentum to prevent overshoot.
- Model tends to overestimate early price declines (e.g., 65–66 range) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for such cases.
- After a strong upward spike (e.g., >70), model often overestimates continuation — apply a 1–2 day lagged mean reversion correction.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to overpredict peak — reduce forecast by 1–3% in the 3–5 day horizon.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.27), model often misreads momentum — use 3-day moving average of true values as a smoothing anchor.
- Avoid forecasting below 65 when sentiment is positive — model underestimates support levels in bullish sentiment.
- If forecasted price dips below 65 and sentiment is positive, assume rebound — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for next 3 days.
